item.content:encoded:
The Madang District Court has convicted and sentenced six men to prison following a major drug bust involving over eight kilograms of marijuana with an estimated street value exceeding K100,000.

Senior Provincial Magistrate Fridolin Kambibel sentenced five of the offenders to five years in prison, with the option of a K5,000 court fine. The sixth offender, 35-year-old Frank Tualai from Sibte village in the Aitape-Lumi District, received a 20-year prison sentence after being found guilty of transporting the bulk of the illegal drugs.

The convictions follow a police operation on June 8, when officers received a tip-off regarding drug movements on public transport. Police intercepted a Route 17A Public Motor Vehicle [PMV] bus around midday at the Puma Service Station in Modilon.

A subsequent search revealed a rainbow-coloured bag containing more than eight kilograms of marijuana packed inside rice bags and smaller bundles.

Madang Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Robert Baim, commended the arresting officers and Prosecutor Senior Constable Eugene Wanai for securing the convictions.

"I commend the arresting officer and my OIC Prosecution Section, Senior Constable Eugene Wanai, for the successful prosecution of this drug case," Chief Supt Baim said. "People know the consequences, yet they keep on committing the offence."

Baim said the court's decision serves as a stern message to those involved in the illicit drug trade. He said police will continue targeting the production, transportation, and sale of illegal drugs across Madang province.

He also urged members of the public to assist law enforcement by reporting drug-related activities within their communities.

item.title: Faith, farming and goodwill drive rural change in Vanimo
item.description: An intensive cross-border agricultural initiative is transforming rural livelihoods in the inland communities of the Vanimo-Green River district of West Sepik. The Indonesian Consulate office in Vanimo has partnered with the local Catholic Church to deliver high-level technical development to remote communities that have long struggled with isolation and lack of market access.
item.content:encoded:
An intensive cross-border agricultural initiative is transforming rural livelihoods in the inland communities of the Vanimo-Green River district of West Sepik.

The Indonesian Consulate office in Vanimo has partnered with the local Catholic Church to deliver high-level technical development to remote communities that have long struggled with isolation and lack of market access.

As part of this historic international collaboration, a leading Indonesian agriculture expert, professor Didik Wisnu Widjajanto, from the Agriculture Faculty of Diponegoro University in Semarang, was flown in directly to conduct a specialized one-day workshop.

The training brought world-class agricultural strategies straight to grassroots growers from the remote Watape and Paipai villages in the Vanimo interior. Farmers received intensive, hands-on training in modern crop management, soil fertility enhancement, and natural pest control strategies.

The workshop directly backs the "Friends of St Francis Agriculture Project," which was founded in 2024 by parish priest Father Martin Prado of the Institute of the Incarnate Word [IVE] Missionary Congregation from Argentina.

Before the project's inception in 2024, inland families faced severe economic and physical hardships. The initiative originally started to help local village mothers avoid grueling, day-long walks through thick jungle mud to Imonda just to sell their fresh produce. Often, after walking these immense distances, the mothers found no buyers and were forced to give away their hard work for free or watch it rot, returning to the village empty-handed and heavily burdened by expensive PMV fares and truck hires.

To restore their dignity and security, Father Martin intervened with a practical solution. He began purchasing all garden crops directly in the village. In exchange, he supplied the mothers with essential household store goods like rice, salt, and soap, saving them from the high expenses and exhaustion of traveling to town markets.

To ensure the long-term sustainability of the initiative, the project has focused heavily on human resource development. Local youth leaders Balthazar Agus and Norman Lenya were sponsored to study professional farming systems overseas, with Agus traveling to Italy for three months and Lenya studying in Surabaya, Indonesia, for two months.

Now serving as the official Project Manager, Agus stated that the advanced knowledge brought in by Professor Widjajanto will help accelerate a major shift in the community, moving them away from a traditional subsistence farming mentality into active, self-sustaining commercial agribusiness.

However, despite its immense impact, the cooperative operates strictly as a non-profit charity that depends entirely on international donor agencies and a dedicated team of unpaid youth volunteers who work out of a sheer love for their community.

Agus revealed that the project faces severe, unavoidable operational hurdles on a weekly basis, including heartbreaking crop rot due to a total lack of cold storage facilities and proper tools. He has issued an urgent call to provincial and national authorities to open their eyes, step in, and officially assist the project with funding, agribusiness equipment, and critical rural road infrastructure repairs.

The Indonesian Consul to Vanimo, Tangkuman Alexander Immanuel, emphasized that this specialized workshop strengthens tangible, strategic, and peaceful relationship-building directly with rural PNG communities.

Meanwhile, Professor Widjajanto said the virgin inland soil of Vanimo-Green River holds enormous agrarian potential for long-term food security if managed with the proper technical strategies.

Local growers from both Watape and Paipai expressed overwhelming joy following the training, stating that receiving world-class knowledge right in their backyard gives them renewed hope for true economic self-reliance.

The rapid growth of the Friends of St Francis Agriculture Project since 2024 stands as a shining example of how faith, international goodwill, and youth empowerment can cooperatively develop remote PNG parishes.

item.title: Magarima DDA commits K1 million for emergency disaster relief
item.description: The Magarima District Development Authority [DDA] has announced a K1 million total emergency disaster relief package to support vulnerable communities across the district in response to the severe drought conditions. The initial allocation of K500,000 was officially committed on Friday by MP and DDA chairman Manase Makiba.
item.content:encoded:
The Magarima District Development Authority [DDA] has announced a K1 million total emergency disaster relief package to support vulnerable communities across the district in response to the severe drought conditions.

The initial allocation of K500,000 was officially committed on Friday by MP and DDA chairman Manase Makiba.

MP Makiba confirmed that a second tranche of K500,000 will be deployed towards the end of the year to maintain continuous assistance as the El Niño climate phenomenon persists.

The decision was formalized immediately following the official swearing-in of the new DDA board members and the formal establishment of the District Disaster Management Committee [DDMC].

"Our people are suffering, and we cannot afford to wait. This K1 million intervention will ensure no family or village is left behind as we navigate this crisis together. Given that the effects of this severe weather pattern are projected to extend into next year, proactive and sustained support is critical," he said.

He said the newly formed district disaster management committee will spearhead a three-pronged emergency operational response which include;

Impact Assessment: Conducting - comprehensive field evaluations across all three Local Level Government (LLG) areas in Magarima to identify high-risk zones.

Community Awareness: Executing public communication drives regarding water conservation, crop management, and resource protection.

Emergency Report Submission: Compiling a detailed status report to present to the Hela Provincial Government and national authorities for further inter-agency support.

​Makiba also stated that relief efforts will strictly prioritize remote, high-altitude villages where subsistence gardens have dried up and natural water sources have depleted entirely due to the prolonged dry spell.

"​Funding will directly facilitate the purchase and logistical delivery of essential supplies, including emergency food rations [rice, flour, and non-perishables]. ​ ​To guarantee equitable access and prevent delays, DDA Chief Executive Officer Simon Olaija confirmed that distribution channels will utilize established grassroots leadership.

"Deliveries will be strictly managed through a combined network of LLG presidents, ward members, and local church leaders."

Olaija urged the people to manage relief supplies responsibly and emphasized the importance of community-wide efforts to protect remaining water reserves and surviving crops throughout the El Niño period.

item.title: Dei district clears decade-long backlog, hands over acquittals
item.description: The Dei District Development Authority in Western Highlands has cleared a 10-year backlog of financial reporting by handing over its acquittals for the 2023 to 2025 period to the Department of Implementation and Rural Development [DIRD]. Dei MP Desmond Kipa presented the financial documents to DIRD Secretary Aihi Vaki in Port Moresby on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Dei District Development Authority in Western Highlands has cleared a 10-year backlog of financial reporting by handing over its acquittals for the 2023 to 2025 period to the Department of Implementation and Rural Development [DIRD].

Dei MP Desmond Kipa presented the financial documents to DIRD Secretary Aihi Vaki in Port Moresby on Wednesday.

The submission makes Dei the 14th district in the country to meet its financial reporting compliance under the Public Financial Management Act.

Kipa, who was elected into office in February following a by-election, said establishing transparency and accountability was his immediate priority upon taking office.

“We discovered that district financial reports had not been submitted since around 2016,” Kipa said.

“With technical assistance from DIRD officers, our administration managed to compile and finalize reports covering 2023, 2024, and 2025.

“This presentation reflects our commitment to transparency, sound financial management, and restoring accountability for public funds delivered for local services.”

Kipa spoke of operational hurdles in rural districts including unreliable electricity, poor telecommunications, and lack of internet access, continue to delay reporting compliance.

However, he welcomed DIRD’s rollout of the digital “Bilum” reporting platform, stating that online submissions would eliminate costly travel and freight expenses.

“Instead of district executives flying to Port Moresby to physically deliver boxes of documents, the digital system allows direct uploads,” he said.

“Funds saved on airfares and accommodation can be redirected toward basic services in the district.”

DIRD Secretary Aihi Vaki commended Kipa and his administration for addressing the long-outstanding reporting failure left by previous leaderships.

Vaki said the department was committed to changing all districts to paperless reporting to cut costs and streamline oversight.

“It is expensive to print, carton, and air-freight stacks of paper to Moresby,” Vaki said.

“The Bilum platform simplifies the process, upskills sub-national staff, and ensures immediate verification of district expenditure.”

Dei DDA chief executive officer Raphael Korldop thanked DIRD technical staff for guiding the district team to ensure the acquittal compilation met statutory requirements.

item.title: Nurturing young minds through books
item.description: Alotau Preparatory School marked the conclusion of National Book Week on Friday, August 7, with a colorful series of activities aimed at promoting a strong reading culture among early learners. item.content:encoded:
Alotau Preparatory School marked the conclusion of National Book Week on Friday, August 7, with a colorful series of activities aimed at promoting a strong reading culture among early learners.

Located in the heart of Alotau town in Milne Bay, the school came alive as students dressed up as their favorite book characters and presented drama performances, poems, riddles, miming, and songs to wrap up the weeklong event.

This year’s National Book Week was observed across the country under the theme "Read a book, Reset your Future".

Teacher-in-Charge Muriel Israel emphasized the necessity of instilling fundamental literacy skills in young children during their early development stages.

"Keep your books close, but keep your dreams closer," Ms. Israel said. "Even though we are closing the weeklong National Book Week celebration, never close your books, as reading is every child's journey to a better life in the future."

She said reading must remain at the core of every learning environment, stating that observances such as National Book Week and Literacy Week should not be the only occasions when students are encouraged to read.

She called for reading to become a continuous daily culture rather than an isolated annual activity.

She said building a consistent reading habit in children requires active support from teachers, parents, and guardians, as daily reading provides the knowledge needed to shape a child’s future prospects.

item.title: PPC Baim appeals to residents to refrain from lawlessness
item.description: Madang's top cop, Superintendent Robert Baim, is urging all residents of Ward 8 in Madang Urban local level government to refrain from all forms of lawlessness, or they risk facing the full brunt of the law. He sounded the warning following two separate attacks on government vehicles travelling the airport road last week.
item.content:encoded:
Madang's top cop, Superintendent Robert Baim, is urging all residents of Ward 8 in Madang Urban local level government to refrain from all forms of lawlessness, or they risk facing the full brunt of the law.

He sounded the warning following two separate attacks on government vehicles travelling the airport road last week.

The first incident occurred midweek to a vehicle belonging to the PNG Maritime College and the second incident in the early hours of Saturday to a vehicle belonging to the Madang Provincial Health Authority.

In the first incident, the driver escaped near death after a bullet, penetrated the glass of the vehicle, a 15- seater bus.

The second incident around 4am on Saturday occurred near Madang Timbers, where the Madang PHA's 15-seater bus was stoned.

Superintendent Baim said police will no longer tolerate unlawful behaviours around this particular area as it is the gateway to Madang.

"Every visitor coming to Madang by air forms their perceptions about the province through Ward 8 as it is the gateway," he said.

"Whatever happens to them upon arrival around this area forms a lasting impression about Madang, and as much as possible, every resident of that area must display their best behaviour at all times.

"The first impression should reflect a province that is safe, peaceful, and welcoming."

He added that Madang's gateway should be remembered for its hospitality and not violence and criminal behaviours.

PPC Baim emphasised that all residents of ward 8, including parents and youths, must cease the habit of stoning vehicles travelling to and fro the airport in the early hours of the morning or at any time at all.

"The criminal act of stoning vehicles not only places innocent lives at risk, but also tarnishes Madang's reputation, discourages tourism and investment, and undermines economic growth and development for the province," Baim said.

item.title: Tubiana marks 125 years of faith
item.description: Archbishop of Rabaul and Metropolitan Bishop of the New Guinea Islands Rochus Tatamai has called on Catholics to renew their personal conviction, reflect on human existence, and allocate more time to prayer. Speaking during mass to conclude three days of worship for the Central Bougainville leg of the 125 Years Jubilee Celebrations at Tubiana Parish in Kieta today, Archbishop Rochus urged believer
item.content:encoded:
Archbishop of Rabaul and Metropolitan Bishop of the New Guinea Islands Rochus Tatamai has called on Catholics to renew their personal conviction, reflect on human existence, and allocate more time to prayer.

Speaking during mass to conclude three days of worship for the Central Bougainville leg of the 125 Years Jubilee Celebrations at Tubiana Parish in Kieta today, Archbishop Rochus urged believers to make themselves available for God's work.

He said while the church celebrates 125 years of history and faith in the region, there is still room for spiritual growth, emphasizing that the future of the church rests on today’s generation.

Archbishop Rochus was joined by Archbishop of Mount Hagen Clement Papa. Both leaders were invited by Bishop of the Bougainville Diocese Dariusz Kaluza to participate in the event.

Priests from local parishes and the Solomon Islands alongside catechists, deacons, religious sisters, and missionaries from across Central Bougainville attended the gathering.

A pilgrim walk from Mangkaki led into the Tubiana Mission grounds earlier in the morning, where thousands gathered for praise and worship.

The Jubilee celebrations commenced in Buin, South Bougainville, last week to mark the arrival of missionaries at Patupatuai in 1903.

The Central Bougainville leg concludes today following services at Pokpok Island on Friday to mark the 1901 arrival of missionaries, and at Mangkaki Point on Saturday, site of the first mission and parish in Bougainville.

The Catholic Church in Bougainville has since expanded to six deaneries and 35 parishes, serving a population of over 200,000 faithful.

The anniversary program now proceeds to Buka in the North region, where three weeks of celebrations will officially draw to a close.

item.title: Popondetta primary school celebrates National Book Week
item.description: Popondetta Primary School joined educational institutions across the country in celebrating National Book Week, held annually during the first week of August. Centering on this year’s theme, "Read a Book, Reset Your Future," students and teachers gathered outdoors to showcase a variety of creative activities.
item.content:encoded:
Popondetta Primary School joined educational institutions across the country in celebrating National Book Week, held annually during the first week of August.

Centering on this year’s theme, "Read a Book, Reset Your Future," students and teachers gathered outdoors to showcase a variety of creative activities.

Preparations took place throughout the week under the direction of special events coordinator Orerea Rex.

During the event, students engaged in writing short stories and original poems, creating thematic drawings, singing performance pieces, and staging short dramatic presentations.

According to Mrs Rex, the main objective of observance is to foster a strong reading culture and inspire continuous learning among students.

To keep this going, every classroom at Popondetta Primary School has established its own dedicated "library corner," stocked with books donated directly by the students themselves.

Complementing the week's festivities, Japan International Cooperation Agency [JICA] volunteer teacher Kitayama Atsuhiro spearheaded a project aimed at building custom bookshelves for each classroom at the school.

Speaking to NBC News, Mr Atsuhiro explained that funding for the initiative was provided by a Japanese organization working in partnership with sponsors from Singapore.

Following the successful implementation at Popondetta Primary School, Mr Atsuhiro plans to extend the bookshelf project to two additional schools in the Northern Province: Crusade Primary School and Bethel Primary School.
